title: Brave Leo adds end-to-end encryption for one open-weight chat model
friendlyTitle: Brave can encrypt some AI chats before they leave your computer
summary: Brave said its Leo assistant can now encrypt prompts on the device before they leave, for chats that use the open-weight GLM 5.3 Flash model. Only an attested hardware enclave, operated by NEAR AI, is meant to decrypt them. The mode is available in Brave Release, Beta and Nightly, and builds on the confidential-computing option Brave announced in November 2025.
friendlySummary: Brave says its Leo assistant can now lock a prompt on your device before sending it, when you use the GLM 5.3 Flash model. Only a sealed computer run by NEAR AI is supposed to unlock it. This is available in the normal Brave browser and in its test versions.
whyItMatters: People who paste medical, legal or work notes into a browser chatbot have a mode where Brave says neither it nor the model host holds a readable copy. It applies to this model and mode, not to every AI feature in the browser, so check which chat you are in before treating a prompt as private.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This is a stronger privacy option for sensitive questions. It covers this model and this mode, not every AI feature in the browser.
